instrument.name: synth
instrument.description: modular DSP synthesizer for macOS and STM32: subtractive, modal/physical and drum machine engines with an effect bus

global.description: master and effect bus, shared by every engine: engine -> chorus -> tape delay -> plate reverb -> master

master.help: master output level (after the effects, before the soft clipper)

chorus_mode.help: chorus: I = slow and deep, II = faster, I+II = both, ensemble = 3-phase string-machine shimmer

chorus_mix.help: chorus wet amount added to the dry sound (width, analog lushness)

delay_mix.help: tape echo level (0 = off): 0.2-0.4 ambient, more for dub

delay_time.help: echo time; changing it bends the repeats like a tape machine. Tempo: 60/bpm x beats

delay_ratio.help: right echo time = left x ratio (1.5 = dotted feel, 0.75 ...); ignored in ping-pong

delay_feedback.help: amount of repeats: 0.3 few, 0.6 long trail, 0.9+ near self-oscillation

delay_tone.help: low-pass inside the loop: each repeat gets darker (tape); 2-4 kHz = warm, 10k+ = digital

delay_drive.help: tape saturation inside the loop: repeats get grainier and compressed

delay_wow.help: tape wow and flutter: pitch wobble of the repeats (0.2 subtle, 0.6+ seasick)

reverb_mix.help: plate reverb level (0 = off): 0.2 room-ish, 0.5 ambient, 0.8+ washed out

reverb_decay.help: tail length: 0.5 ~1.8 s, 0.85 ~5 s, 0.93 ~10 s, 0.97+ endless

reverb_damping.help: high-frequency loss in the tail: lower = darker, softer

reverb_predelay.help: gap before the reverb: keeps the dry sound clear

reverb_freeze.help: freeze: the current tail holds forever and new sound stays dry on top (CC 69)

tempo.help: tempo of the internal clock (synced LFOs, MSEGs and delay); ignored while following MIDI clock

clock.help: internal = the tempo parameter; midi = follow the MIDI clock of a sequencer or drum machine

delay_sync.help: off = delay_time in seconds; a division = the echo follows the tempo (1/8d = dotted eighth)

tuning.help: temperament: equal; just (pure thirds and fifths, from the root); pythagorean; quarter-comma meantone; werckmeister III; custom (tune_0..tune_11, e.g. from a Scala file with tools/scala_to_patch.py)

tuning_root.help: the note the tuning is built on (its intervals are pure from there)

tune_0.help: custom tuning: offset of degree 0 above the root

tune_1.help: custom tuning: offset of degree 1 above the root

tune_2.help: custom tuning: offset of degree 2 above the root

tune_3.help: custom tuning: offset of degree 3 above the root

tune_4.help: custom tuning: offset of degree 4 above the root

tune_5.help: custom tuning: offset of degree 5 above the root

tune_6.help: custom tuning: offset of degree 6 above the root

tune_7.help: custom tuning: offset of degree 7 above the root

tune_8.help: custom tuning: offset of degree 8 above the root

tune_9.help: custom tuning: offset of degree 9 above the root

tune_10.help: custom tuning: offset of degree 10 above the root

tune_11.help: custom tuning: offset of degree 11 above the root

a4_hz.help: concert pitch: the frequency of A4, for every part and every tuning (432, 440, 442, 415 baroque...)

out_filter.help: a filter on the instrument's output, before the effects: off, low-pass, high-pass or band-pass (12 dB)

out_cutoff.help: cutoff (or centre) of the output filter

out_resonance.help: resonance of the output filter: 0 = smooth, 1 = sharp peak

crush_bits.help: resolution of the instrument's output, its steps spanning the nominal level (-12 dBFS): 24 = clean, 8 = grainy, 2-4 = broken digital

crush_rate.help: sample rate of the instrument's output (sample and hold): 48 kHz = clean, lower = metallic aliasing, a few hundred Hz = data noise

saturation.help: a saturation on the whole mix, after the master level: soft (tanh, glue), tube (asymmetric: even harmonics, warmth), hard (cubic clip: brighter, flat tops)

saturation_drive.help: gain into the saturation, the peaks kept at the same level (denser, so louder, as it squares them): 0-6 dB = glue, 12 dB and more = audibly driven

saturation_tone.help: a low-pass after the saturation: 20 kHz = open, lower = darker, tape-like

limiter.help: a look-ahead peak limiter, last on the mix (1.5 ms of latency): no peak goes past the ceiling, no clipping

limiter_gain.help: gain into the limiter: louder, the peaks held at the ceiling (beyond 6-8 dB the mix starts to pump)

limiter_ceiling.help: the highest peak out of the limiter, in dBFS

limiter_release.help: time to come back after a peak: short = loud but grainy on bass, long = smooth but pumping

phaser_mix.help: phaser amount: 0 = off, 1 = half dry, half phased (the deepest notches)

phaser_rate.help: speed of the sweep: 0.05-0.5 Hz = slow swirl, several Hz = a vibrato-like warble

phaser_center.help: middle of the sweep: low = throaty, high = airy

phaser_depth.help: width of the sweep, up to 4 octaves (2 each side of the centre)

phaser_feedback.help: resonance of the notches: 0 = gentle, high = a sharp, singing sweep; negative = the peaks move between the notches

phaser_stages.help: all-pass stages: 4 = the classic small phaser (2 notches), more = more notches, a denser swirl

flanger_mix.help: flanger amount: 0 = off, 1 = half dry, half delayed (the deepest notches, the jet)

flanger_rate.help: speed of the sweep: 0.05-0.3 Hz = the slow jet, faster = a wobble

flanger_delay.help: the longest delay of the sweep: short = high, metallic notches, long = lower, towards a chorus

flanger_depth.help: how far the sweep goes, down to a twentieth of the delay

flanger_feedback.help: resonance: high = metallic, ringing; negative = hollow (the resonances at the odd multiples of half the delay's frequency)

tape.help: a worn tape machine on the whole signal: pitch that wanders, soft saturation, dull highs, hiss

tape_wow.help: wow: slow pitch wander of everything (0.2 alive, 0.5 worn cassette, 1 = about 0.5 %, seasick)

tape_flutter.help: flutter: fast pitch tremble (about 7 Hz), the grain of a cheap transport

tape_drive.help: level onto the tape: 0 clean, 0.3 rounded peaks and glue, 0.7 and more compressed and gritty (level kept)

tape_hiss.help: tape hiss under the sound (0 = none; it stays after the notes, like a real machine left running)

tape_tone.help: loss of highs: 12 kHz and more a good machine, 6-9 kHz a cassette, 2-4 kHz a tape left in the sun

reverb_shimmer.help: shimmer: the tail comes back into the reverb transposed, so it climbs and glows (0.3 a halo, 0.6 an organ of light, 1 = it keeps rising); needs a long decay

reverb_shimmer_pitch.help: interval of the shimmer: an octave up (the classic), a fifth up (stacks into chords), a twelfth up, or an octave down (the tail sinks)

part.description: mixer strip and routing of each of the 8 parts (multitimbral; a patch sets the part it is loaded on)

part_pan.help: part balance (-1 left, +1 right; centre keeps both sides at full level)

part_channel.help: MIDI channel the part listens to (omni = all)

part_key_lo.help: lowest MIDI note played by the part (keyboard splits)

part_key_hi.help: highest MIDI note played by the part

part_transpose.help: transposition of the notes the part receives

part_fx_send.help: share of the part going through the effect bus (chorus, delay, reverb); the rest bypasses it

part_mpe.help: MPE: each note on its own channel (2..16) with its own pitch bend, pressure and slide (CC 74); channel 1 stays global. Pressure and slide are per-voice modulation sources

part_mpe_bend.help: per-note pitch-bend range of an MPE controller

modulation.description: per part, every engine: 8 macros, 2 LFOs (free or tempo-synced), 2 MSEGs, MIDI sources, 8 routes onto the engine's realtime parameters (amount in fractions of the destination's range); route destinations are engine parameter names

wander.help: slow random drift of the eight macros, each on its own walk: the sound moves by itself through what its macros reach and never comes back the same way (0.2 alive, 0.5 always changing, 1 = up to a third of each macro's travel)

wander_rate.help: how often the walks change direction: 0.02 Hz glacial, 0.08 Hz a slow breath, 0.5 Hz and more restless

va.description: subtractive virtual analog: 2 oscillators (sine/saw/pulse/tri, each a unison of up to 16 detuned voices spread in stereo) + noise -> two filter slots in series or parallel (state-variable, formant, screaming 2-pole) -> amp; amp and filter ADSR, global LFO, 3 desynchronized per-voice detune LFOs, analog drift (8 voices)

osc1_wave.help: osc 1 waveform: saw = bright/brassy, pulse = hollow (square at pw 0.5), tri = soft flute, sine = pure; osc1_unison stacks detuned copies of it

osc1_semi.help: osc 1 transposition in semitones (7 = fifth, 12 = octave)

osc1_detune.help: osc 1 fine tune; detuning against osc 2 gives beating/chorus (5-12 cents = lush)

osc1_pw.help: osc 1 pulse width (pulse wave only): 0.5 square, small/large values thin and nasal

osc2_oct.help: osc 2 octave shift (-1 = sub oscillator for bass weight)

osc2_detune.help: osc 2 fine tune (default +7 cents: gentle chorus)

noise_level.help: white noise level: breath, air, percussive transients (with short amp envelope)

filter_mode.help: filter type: lp = classic subtractive, bp = nasal/vocal, hp = thin, notch = phasey, formant = vowels (cutoff 1 kHz = adult voice, filter_character = vowel a..u), scream = screaming 2-pole low-pass (filter_character = drive)

cutoff.help: filter cutoff (base, before envelope/keytrack/velocity/LFO): main brightness control

resonance.help: filter Q: 0.7 neutral, 2-5 vocal peak, 8-25 squelchy/whistling (acid)

fenv_amount.help: filter envelope depth in octaves (+4 = big 'pew', negative = inverted sweep)

keytrack.help: cutoff follows the keyboard (1 = one octave per octave): keeps high notes bright

vel_cutoff.help: octaves of cutoff lost at low velocity: expressive brightness

amp_attack.help: amp attack: <5 ms percussive, 20-80 ms soft, >0.3 s swelling pad

amp_decay.help: amp decay time to the sustain level

amp_release.help: amp release after note-off: short = tight, long = ambient tail

fenv_attack.help: filter envelope attack (slow = filter opens progressively)

fenv_decay.help: filter envelope decay: 0.1-0.25 s = plucky/acid, 1-3 s = evolving

lfo_rate.help: global LFO rate (vibrato 4.5-6.5 Hz, slow movement 0.1-1 Hz)

lfo_pitch.help: LFO -> pitch depth in semitones (0.1-0.3 = vibrato, more = siren)

lfo_cutoff.help: LFO -> cutoff depth in octaves (wah / slow breathing)

lfo_pwm.help: LFO -> pulse width (PWM: animated, string-ensemble-like pulse sound)

wheel_vibrato.help: extra vibrato depth (semitones) added by the mod wheel (CC 1)

volume.help: engine volume in dB (voices already sit at -18 dBFS each)

drift.help: analog drift: slow random wander of each oscillator (standard deviation, cents; the filter follows a little)

pan_spread.help: random stereo position per voice (0 = mono center, 1 = wide)

lfo2_rate.help: per-voice detune LFO rate (0.05-0.5 Hz = slow shimmering beating)

lfo2_detune.help: LFO 2 depth on osc 2 detune in cents: moving chorus/beating, the classic lush detuned pad

lfo2_spread.help: per-voice randomness of phase and rate of LFOs 2, 3, 4 (+/-40 % at 1): chord notes beat independently

lfo2_rate_mod.help: LFO 1 -> rate of LFOs 2/3/4 in octaves, in opposite directions (LFO of LFO: beating speeds up/slows down, LFOs drift apart)

lfo2_depth_mod.help: LFO 1 -> depth of LFOs 2/3/4 (LFO of LFO: the detune swells and settles)

lfo3_rate.help: per-voice LFO 3 rate (default ~0.76 x LFO 2: never in sync)

lfo3_detune.help: LFO 3 depth on osc 1 detune in cents: second, desynchronized beating layer

lfo4_rate.help: per-voice LFO 4 rate (default ~0.24 x LFO 2: very slow)

lfo4_detune.help: LFO 4 depth on the whole voice pitch in cents: chord notes slowly drift against each other (tape-like)

osc1_unison.help: osc 1 unison: copies of the oscillator sounding together, detuned and spread (1 = a single oscillator; 3-5 = thick, 7-9 = a classic stack, 12-16 = a wall; each voice costs an oscillator)

osc1_unison_detune.help: how far the outermost unison voice is detuned, in cents; the inner voices stay closer (10-20 = subtle chorus, 25-40 = lush, 60+ = wide, trance)

osc1_unison_blend.help: level of the side voices against the centre one, the loudness kept: 0 = the centre alone, 1 = every voice as loud

osc1_unison_width.help: stereo width of the unison voices: 0 = mono (cheaper: one filter per voice), 1 = from hard left to hard right (mono on a board built with VA_STEREO 0)

osc2_unison.help: osc 2 unison: copies of the oscillator sounding together, detuned and spread (1 = a single oscillator; 3-5 = thick, 7-9 = a classic stack, 12-16 = a wall; each voice costs an oscillator)

osc2_unison_detune.help: how far the outermost unison voice is detuned, in cents; the inner voices stay closer (10-20 = subtle chorus, 25-40 = lush, 60+ = wide, trance)

osc2_unison_blend.help: level of the side voices against the centre one, the loudness kept: 0 = the centre alone, 1 = every voice as loud

osc2_unison_width.help: stereo width of the unison voices: 0 = mono (cheaper: one filter per voice), 1 = from hard left to hard right (mono on a board built with VA_STEREO 0)

unison_motion.help: a slow, desynchronized LFO on each unison voice's detune, in cents: the stack breathes and shimmers

unison_motion_rate.help: average rate of the unison motion LFOs (each voice gets 0.6-1.4x this rate)

pitch_env.help: pitch envelope: the note starts this many semitones away and glides back (+24..+36 with 30-60 ms = kick drum, +7..+12 = snare/tom snap, -12..-24 = laser zap)

pitch_env_decay.help: time constant of the pitch envelope

voice_mode.help: poly = chords; mono = one voice, last note wins, every note retriggers the envelopes; legato = one voice, overlapping notes slide without retriggering (acid lines, leads, basses)

glide.help: portamento time (constant time, like an RC glide): 0.03-0.08 s = acid slide, 0.2-0.5 s = lazy lead

glide_mode.help: always = every note glides from the previous one; legato = only overlapping (tied) notes glide

filter_character.help: filter_mode formant: the vowel (0 a, 0.25 e, 0.5 i, 0.75 o, 1 u); scream: drive into the screaming feedback

filter2_mode.help: second filter: off, or a type like filter 1 (follows the same envelope, keytracking and modulation)

filter2_cutoff.help: second filter cutoff (formant: 1 kHz = adult voice)

filter_routing.help: series = filter 1 then filter 2 (e.g. hp then lp = band); parallel = both on the oscillators, mixed (e.g. two formants = a vowel pair, lp + hp = notch-like)

oversample.help: oversampling of the scream filter character (the others are linear): 1x lightest, 2x default, 4x cleanest screaming resonance

tolerance.help: static offset of each oscillator, drawn once (the tolerance of its parts): up to this many cents

drift_time.help: time constant of the drift: how slowly each oscillator wanders

jitter.help: phase jitter: a little white noise on each oscillator's pitch, irregular beats (keep it very light)

modal.description: modal synthesis: banks of up to 32 resonators per note, struck (hammer/mallet + noise) or bowed (noise), with stiff string (piano: inharmonicity, unison strings, double decay), bar, marimba, bell, membrane, bowl and tube models (12 voices)

model.help: resonator: harmonic = ideal string, string = stiff string (piano; see inharmonicity), bar = glockenspiel, marimba, bell = church bell (minor-third tierce, low hum), membrane = drum/gong, bowl = singing bowl/glass, tube = hollow odd harmonics

modes.help: number of resonant modes (more = richer and costlier): 6-8 for bars and bells, 24-32 for a piano; table models (bar..bowl) use at most 16

stretch.help: bends the mode ratios (ratio^(1+stretch)): invents new, unheard materials; 0 = the physical model

decay.help: ring time (T60) of the fundamental: 0.3 s wood, 2-4 s metal bar, 10+ s bell or bowl

damping.help: how much faster high modes die (0 = all equal, metallic shimmer; 2+ = soft, wooden)

release.help: ring time after note-off (a damper); set >= decay to let notes ring freely

brightness.help: level of high modes vs low ones: 0 = dark and round, 1 = bright and glassy

position.help: strike position (0 = off): 0.5 hits the middle and cancels even modes, 0.1-0.2 = edge, hollow comb

hardness.help: mallet hardness: 0 = felt (5 ms contact, dull), 1 = metal (0.15 ms, sharp attack)

noise.help: noise burst in the strike: scrape, breath, chiff

vel_brightness.help: soft notes are darker (like a real mallet)

bow.help: continuous noise excitation while the key is held: bowed glass, singing bowls, endless drones

bow_attack.help: time for the bow to reach full level

variation.help: random per-note detune of each mode: every strike is slightly different, beating partials

pan_spread.help: random stereo position per note (0 = centre)

inharmonicity.help: string stiffness B (model string): partials sharpen as k*sqrt(1+B k^2); 1e-4 bass strings, 3e-4..1e-3 piano middle, 5e-3+ bright treble / bell-like

unison.help: 2 strings per partial (first 8 partials) detuned by this many cents, one decaying faster: piano beating and double decay (prompt sound + long aftersound); 0.5-2 cents for a piano

decay_keytrack.help: high notes ring shorter: decay x 2^(-keytrack x octaves above C4); ~0.8-1 for a piano

aftersound.help: unison double decay contrast: 0 = two similar strings (soft, even ring), 1 = a loud fast-decaying string plus a quiet long one (marked piano attack then long aftersound)

tension.help: string nonlinearity: a loud note stretches the string and raises its tension, mostly through the low partials: every partial starts sharp and glides down together as the note decays (the fundamental's envelope drives the others' pitch). 0 = linear; 0.3-0.6 = piano (a few cents), 1 = gong-like

drums.description: drum machine, 12 instruments on GM notes plus a melodic bass drum (36 kick, 37 rim, 38 snare, 39 clap, 42 closed hat, 46 open hat, 41/45/48 toms, 49 cymbal, 56 cowbell, 75 clave); kits: analog (early-80s analog machine) and hybrid (mid-80s analog/sample machine), glitch, trap; under the map (notes 0..34) a melodic bass drum that slides between held notes; per-instrument level, tune, decay, tone

kit.help: analog = deep booming kick, soft round snare, silky metallic hats (electro, hip-hop, ambient); hybrid = punchy clicky kick, bright snappy snare, gritty hats and rides (house, techno); glitch = digital microsound: sub sine pulses, single-sample clicks, pure high beeps, white and decimated data noise, modem chirps (minimal, glitch, installation); trap = short punchy kick, tight cracking snare, layered roomy clap, crisp bright hats for fast rolls

accent.help: how much velocity changes level, decay and brightness (0 = every hit equal)

drive.help: saturation of the whole kit: glue and grit, louder transients become rounder

stereo.help: spread of the instruments in the stereo field (0 = mono like the original machines)

kick_tune.help: kick pitch (default ~49 Hz analog, ~52 Hz hybrid)

kick_decay.help: kick length: 0.3 = tight, 1 = default, 3+ = long sub boom

kick_tone.help: click / attack amount (hybrid: beater click and noise)

snare_tone.help: snappy: 0 = mostly drum body, 1 = mostly wires

ohat_decay.help: open hi-hat length (choked by the closed hat)

bass_tune.help: bass drum transposition (it plays at its note's pitch, notes 0..34)

bass_decay.help: bass drum length: 1 = about 2 s, up to 5x

bass_tone.help: drive: 0 = a clean sine, 1 = a growling, saturated boom

glide.help: bass drum slide: a note played while the previous one is held slides from its pitch over this time

mono.description: classic monosynth (the early-70s portable one, panel by panel): 3 free-running oscillators with footage and 6 waveforms, osc 3 as modulator, white / pink noise, mixer that overloads and takes the output back in, 24 dB self-oscillating ladder (2x oversampled), ADS contours, modulation mix (osc 3 or filter contour, noise or LFO), glide, legato, note priority

osc1_range.help: osc 1 footage: 32' (two octaves down) .. 2' (two octaves up), 8' = the played note; lo = five octaves under 32', sub-audio (a modulator)

osc1_wave.help: osc 1 waveform: tri soft, shark (triangle-sawtooth) warm, saw bright, square hollow, wide/narrow pulse nasal

osc2_range.help: osc 2 footage: 32' (two octaves down) .. 2' (two octaves up), 8' = the played note; lo = five octaves under 32', sub-audio (a modulator)

osc2_wave.help: osc 2 waveform: tri soft, shark (triangle-sawtooth) warm, saw bright, square hollow, wide/narrow pulse nasal

osc2_detune.help: osc 2 frequency: a few hundredths = fat beating, 7 = a fifth, -5 = a fourth

osc3_range.help: osc 3 footage: 32' (two octaves down) .. 2' (two octaves up), 8' = the played note; lo = five octaves under 32', sub-audio (a modulator)

osc3_wave.help: osc 3 waveform: as osc 1 and 2, but a reverse sawtooth (rsaw) replaces the shark, for modulation

osc3_detune.help: osc 3 frequency (as a modulator with keytrack off: low ranges give LFO rates)

osc3_keytrack.help: off = osc 3 ignores the keyboard (drone, or LFO for the mod wheel when its range is 32')

mixer_drive.help: how hard the mixer hits the filter: thicker, compressed, warmer (the famous overdrive)

cutoff.help: filter cutoff: the main tone knob

emphasis.help: filter emphasis (resonance); ~0.95 self-oscillates into a pure sine that tracks the keyboard

release.help: on = both contours release with their decay time after key-up; off = short release

glide.help: portamento: the time to reach the new note (1 ms = off); exponential, as the original's RC lag

voice_mode.help: legato = contours retrigger only after all keys are released (the original behaviour); mono = every note

mod_mix.help: modulation mix: 0 = only source A (mod_a: osc 3 or the filter contour), 1 = only source B (mod_b: noise or the LFO), in between both; the mod wheel sets how much of it is applied

mod_pitch.help: mod wheel -> oscillator pitch depth (semitones at full wheel)

mod_cutoff.help: mod wheel -> filter cutoff depth (octaves at full wheel)

drift.help: analog drift: slow random wander of each oscillator (standard deviation, cents)

velocity.help: velocity -> loudness and brightness (the original had none)

bend_range.help: pitch-bend range (the original wheel: 7, a fifth)

osca_pulse.help: osc A pulse on/off (both = saw + pulse summed)

pm_pw_a.help: poly-mod modulates osc A pulse width

unison.help: all voices on one note: huge mono leads and basses

wt.description: wavetable synth (modern wavetable spirit): 2 wavetable oscillators with position morphing, unison and warps (sync, bend, mirror, FM, ring), sub, noise, SVF or ladder filter, distortion, 2 envelopes, 2 LFOs, 6-slot modulation matrix, mono/legato/glide (8 voices)

a_table.help: wavetable: basic (sine>tri>saw>square), pwm, sync, harmonics (additive), vowel (a-e-i-o-u), fold, growl (phase modulation), resonant, digital (random spectra)

a_position.help: position in the table: morphs smoothly between its frames (modulate it for movement)

a_warp_mode.help: phase warp: sync (hard sync, brighter), bend (squeezes the cycle), mirror (forward then backward), fm (phase modulated by osc B; on osc B: by the sub), ring (multiplied by the same source)

a_level.help: oscillator level in the mix (0 still works as an FM/ring source)

a_unison.help: stacked detuned copies (thickness; cost grows with the count)

a_detune.help: unison spread: outermost copies at +/- this (10-25 = lush, 50+ = huge)

b_table.help: wavetable: basic (sine>tri>saw>square), pwm, sync, harmonics (additive), vowel (a-e-i-o-u), fold, growl (phase modulation), resonant, digital (random spectra)

b_position.help: position in the table: morphs smoothly between its frames (modulate it for movement)

filter_type.help: off, 12 dB state-variable (lp/bp/hp/notch), 24 dB ladder low-pass with drive, or a comb: cutoff = its tuning (keytrack 1 = on the note), resonance = feedback, drive = damping of the repeats; comb = all harmonics, comb_neg = hollow (odd harmonics an octave down). Move the cutoff slowly: the comb wanders. formant: vowels (cutoff 1 kHz = adult voice, drive = vowel a..u, resonance = sharpness); scream: screaming 2-pole low-pass (drive = saturation)

drive.help: input saturation of the lp24 ladder (2x oversampled)

env2_attack.help: modulation envelope (use it in the matrix) attack

env2_sustain.help: modulation envelope (use it in the matrix) sustain

lfo2_retrig.help: LFO 2 restarts on each note (off = free running, voices drift apart)

dist_tone.help: low-pass after the distortion: lower tames the fizz

dist_mix.help: distorted signal against the clean one (parallel distortion keeps the body)

dist_place.help: post: after the filter (the filter shapes, the distortion bites); pre: before it (the filter tames the distortion, classic for growling basses)

sub_route.help: filter: the sub goes through the filter and the distortion with the oscillators; direct: it joins after them, clean and steady under a growling or vowel-filtered bass

drone.description: drone machine: each note an endless drone of wandering harmonic partials, a warm body of saws, air on the harmonics and rare sparkles; temperature (glacial .. warm), density, motion, depth, brightness, sparkle, width; envelopes up to 3 minutes (8 voices)

temperature.help: glacial (0: pure glassy partials, high whistling air, bright bells) .. warm (1: dark partials, a body of detuned saws, low breathy air)

density.help: how many partials sound (1 .. 12) and how much air: a lone sine .. a wall

motion.help: speed of every drift: 0 = almost still (walks over ~2 min), 1 = alive (~3 s)

depth.help: size of the drifts: partial levels (up to +/-9 dB), pitches (up to +/-8 cents), body cut-off, air

brightness.help: spectral tilt of the partials and cut-off of the body

sparkle.help: how often a high harmonic rings out of a note (0 = never, 1 = about 10 a minute)

width.help: stereo spread of the partials, each wandering in its own place

body_level.help: level of the body (detuned saws in a low-pass), faded in by temperature

air_level.help: level of the air (noise in band-passes on the note's harmonics)

amp_attack.help: fade in of a note (up to 3 minutes)

amp_release.help: fade out of a note (up to 3 minutes)

air_tone.help: height of the air's bands: lower = a muffled rumble of wind and waves, higher = a hiss

air_reso.help: resonance of the air's bands: 1 = as the temperature sets it (whistling when cold), 0 = wide and soft

micro.description: precision sines: per-sample envelopes, fixed or keyed pitch, pitch envelope, second sine, sub, click, noise layer with its own gate, low layer (a sub with its own sample-exact envelope, pitch drop and gate), tone bursts, ratchets, gate patterns (8 voices)

voice_mode.help: poly, mono (every note retriggers) or legato (overlapping notes glide without retriggering)

pitch_mode.help: key: the note sets the pitch; fixed: every note plays `freq` (the note only triggers)

glide.help: glide time in the mono and legato modes (arrives within 1 % after this time; the bottom = off)

phase.help: start phase of every hit: 0 = soft start from silence, 90 = a deliberate click

phase_reset.help: on: every hit restarts the sines at `phase` (exact, repeatable); off: free running

sine_level.help: level of the main sine (the bottom = off: the click or the second sine alone)

pitch_amount.help: start of the pitch envelope above the note (a kick: +24 .. +48), falling to the note

pitch_time.help: time of the pitch envelope's fall, exact

pitch_curve.help: shape of the pitch fall: 0 linear (in semitones), > 0 fast then slow (a kick), < 0 slow then fast

env_mode.help: gate: the note-off starts the release; one_shot: attack, hold and decay always run to the end (drums)

amp_attack.help: attack time, exact (the bottom = one sample)

amp_hold.help: time held at full level after the attack (the bottom = none)

amp_decay.help: decay time to the sustain level, exact

attack_curve.help: shape of the attack: 0 linear, > 0 fast then slow, < 0 slow then fast

decay_curve.help: shape of the decay and the release: 0 linear, > 0 fast then slow (analog), < 0 slow then fast (a gate)

velocity.help: velocity to level: 0 = every hit equal, 1 = full range

osc2_level.help: level of the second sine (the bottom = off)

osc2_mode.help: ratio: a frequency ratio to the main sine; hz: an offset in Hz (exact beating)

osc2_ratio.help: frequency ratio of the second sine (ratio mode)

osc2_offset.help: frequency offset of the second sine (hz mode): the two sines beat this many times a second

osc2_split.help: on: the main sine (and sub, click) on the left, the second on the right (beating heard between the ears)

osc2_pitch_env.help: the pitch envelope moves the second sine too

sub_level.help: level of the sub sine (the bottom = off)

sub_octave.help: the sub one or two octaves below the main sine

drive.help: saturation of the main sine, sub and click (2x oversampled tanh): harmonics a small speaker can play

click_mode.help: a click on every hit: an impulse through a low-pass, or a noise burst through a band-pass

click_decay.help: length of the noise burst (time to -60 dB)

burst.help: tone burst: every hit plays exactly this many cycles of the main sine, then the sines stop (0 = off)

ratchet.help: hits per note: the note repeats this many times (1 = off)

ratchet_hz.help: repeat rate when not on the tempo

ratchet_decay.help: level change at each repeat (< 0: dying away, > 0: growing toward full level)

gate_div.help: length of a step in sync mode

gate_hz.help: steps per second in free mode

gate_pattern.help: the pattern as 16 bits, step 1 = the lowest bit (43690 = every other step, from step 2)

gate_depth.help: how far a closed step cuts the sound (1 = silence)

gate_edge.help: time of each gate edge (the bottom = one sample: hard, digital)

noise_level.help: level of the noise layer (the bottom = off); it bypasses the drive

noise_type.help: white; stepped: a new random value `noise_rate` times a second (digital grain); periodic: a 7-bit shift register clocked at `noise_rate`, a metallic buzz at noise_rate / 127

noise_rate.help: clock of the stepped and periodic noises (no band limiting: the aliasing is the sound)

noise_q.help: resonance of the noise filter (high = a narrow, whistling band)

noise_env.help: amp: the noise follows the amplitude envelope; hit: its own decay from every hit; step: its own decay, restarted on every step where its gate opens (a tick per step)

noise_decay.help: length of the noise's own decay (hit and step modes; time to -60 dB)

noise_pattern.help: the noise's own pattern, 16 bits, step 1 = the lowest bit (21845 = every other step, from step 1)

low_mode.help: fixed: always at `low_freq`; note: the note played, brought into the octave that starts at `low_freq` (any key gives a low in the same range)

low_freq.help: frequency of the low layer (fixed), or the bottom of its octave (note)

low_phase.help: phase every hit starts at: 0 = from zero, soft; 90 = from the top, a click of its own

low_drop.help: how far above its frequency every hit starts (the punch)

low_drop_time.help: time of the fall to its frequency

low_attack.help: attack of the low layer (the bottom = one sample)

low_hold.help: time at full level before the decay

low_curve.help: curve of the decay: 0 = a straight line, towards 1 = a fast fall then a long tail, towards -1 = held then cut

havoc.description: noise machine with a wide palette: four generators, each one of sixteen processes (feedback sine, logistic map, integer formula, dust into a resonator, band of noise, pulsar train, cellular automaton, swarm of sines, random jumping tone, clipped random walk, chatter of bleeps, electronic faults, formant voice, data transmission, model neuron, aliased saw) with its own pitch, rot, life (steady, bursts, pulse, swell) and place, modulating each other in a ring (FM, ring), then two processors (filter, comb, fold, crush, ring, chop, stutter, octave divider, warp, bit mangle); the output can feed back into every frequency and the machine can mutate while it plays (1 voice, notes slide the machine)

glide.help: time for the generators that follow the note to slide to a new note played while another is held

velocity.help: velocity to level: 0 = every note equal, 1 = full range

width.help: how far the generators are spread to their places (0 = all in the middle)

feedback.help: the machine's output modulates the frequency of every generator: a little roughens, a lot howls and collapses into chaos

mutate.help: how often the machine changes itself while it plays: 0 = never, 0.5 = about once a second, 1 = thirteen times a second. A mutation gives one generator, at random, other shapes and another pitch

mutate_depth.help: size of the mutations: how far the shapes and the pitch (2 octaves at most) are thrown; above the middle a mutation can also change the generator's process

dark.help: a low-pass on the whole machine, after the processors: 0 = open, 0.5 = 1.6 kHz, 1 = 140 Hz, only the weight is left

x1_type.help: processor on the sum of the generators. lp, bp, hp: a filter, p1 = cutoff (30 Hz .. 17 kHz), p2 = resonance. comb: p1 = its pitch (30 Hz .. 7.7 kHz), p2 = feedback (negative below the middle). fold: a wavefolder, p1 = drive, p2 = asymmetry. crush: p1 = lower sampling rate, p2 = fewer bits. ring: multiplied by a sine, p1 = its frequency (1 Hz .. 8 kHz), p2 = phase between left and right. chop: a periodic gate, p1 = rate (0.5 .. 32 Hz), p2 = share of the time it is open. stutter: now and then the last instants repeat as if stuck, p1 = length of the fragment (2 .. 42 ms), p2 = share of the time stuck. sub: a square one octave below whatever comes in (p1 towards 1: two octaves), at the level of the input, p2 = from dull to buzzing; mix adds it under the sound. warp: frequency modulation of the whole sound by a sine, p1 = its frequency (0.5 Hz .. 1 kHz), p2 = depth. mangle: operations on the bits of every sample, p1 = which (exclusive or, rotation, bits killed, bits reversed), p2 = the mask or amount

x1_p1.help: first control of this processor (see its type)

x1_p2.help: second control of this processor (see its type)

g1_type.help: process of this generator. tone: a sine, a = phase feedback (sine, saw, noise), b = a second detuned sine. logistic: the logistic map clocked at the pitch, a = from a period-2 buzz to chaos, b = stepped to smooth. byte: an integer formula on a counter (8-bit digital melodies and noise), a = formula, b = its constant. dust: random impulses (the pitch is their number per second) into a resonator, a = its frequency, b = its ring. wind: a band of noise at the pitch, a = from wide to a whistle, b = gusts. pulsar: a train of short sine bursts, a = their frequency (a formant), b = their length. cell: a cellular automaton of 32 cells read as a wave and stepped every period, a = the rule (0..255), b = smoothing. swarm: eight sines wandering around the pitch, a = how far, b = how fast. computer: a tone that jumps to random pitches, a = range, b = speed. rumble: a random walk, a = fold, b = only the peaks pass (crackle). bleep: a chatter of short notes, some gliding, some square, with rests, a = how far they go and glide, b = notes per second. glitch: electronic faults, one after the other (a stuck loop of bits, a burst of bit noise, a whine, a gap), a = from buzzing loops to noise, b = faults per second. talk: a voice speaking no language (vowels, hisses, stops through three formants; the pitch is the voice's), a = how fast it speaks, b = from voiced to whispered. modem: a data transmission (carrier, preambles, bursts of random symbols, gaps), a = symbols per second (20 .. 640), b = 2, 4 or 8 tones. neuron: a model neuron firing (the pitch is its speed), a = from regular spikes to chattering bursts, b = input current and its noise. alias: a staircase saw pushed past the Nyquist frequency, a = how far (1 .. 64 times the pitch), b = from 256 steps to 2

g1_pitch.help: pitch of this generator, in semitones from the note (or from middle C when it does not track): -96 = 1 Hz, a rhythm; +60 = 8 kHz

g1_track.help: on: this generator follows the note; off: it stays where its pitch puts it

g1_a.help: first shape control of this generator (see its process)

g1_b.help: second shape control of this generator (see its process)

g1_fm.help: frequency modulation of this generator by the one before it (the first by the last)

g1_ring.help: ring modulation of this generator by the one before it: at 1 it sounds only when the other does

g1_life.help: how this generator lives in time: steady, bursts (on and off at random), pulse (a periodic decaying hit), swell (a slow random breath)

g1_life_rate.help: rate of the bursts, the pulse or the swell

g1_life_shape.help: bursts: share of the time it is on; pulse: length of the hit; swell: depth of the breath

g1_level.help: output level of this generator (at 0 it can still modulate the next one)

g1_pan.help: place of this generator, left to right

g1_lfo_rate.help: rate of this generator's own oscillator, which moves its two shape controls: a at this rate, b at 0.62 of it, so the pair never repeats; give every generator another rate

g1_lfo_a.help: how far the oscillator moves a (0 = not at all)

g1_lfo_b.help: how far the oscillator moves b (0 = not at all)

g1_rot.help: this generator resampled at a lower and lower rate and on fewer and fewer bits (down to 270 Hz and 1 bit), with no filter: its aliases then go into whatever it modulates
